guest.bio_context: Logan transitioned from law enforcement early in his career to the construction and safety sector. He began as a safety officer and first aid officer in a distribution warehouse before moving into construction, where he became CSO at Scott Construction—notably the first company he encountered with a mental health committee. He was later CSO at a jobsite connected through Nightingale Electrical before his current promotion to Field Safety Supervisor at West Group.

pending_qa.r: West Group's mental health program called Homeward Health included a questionnaire that revealed Logan was suffering from extreme depression. He stated: 'through West Group, they have a mental health program called Homeward Health. And they had a questionnaire on that. So I did the questionnaire and I was told that I was suffering from extreme depression.'

pending_qa.q: What connection exists between untreated mental illness and substance abuse risk in the trades?
pending_qa.r: Logan emphasized that depression can become a gateway to substance abuse if left unaddressed. He stated: 'I find with depression or any mental illness, it's a gateway to substance abuse. Yeah. You're trying to find that one thing that takes away your depression or your mental health, and it's easy, very easy to find it at the bottom of a bottle.'

pending_qa.q: How does volunteering and service to others work as a therapeutic intervention for depression?
pending_qa.r: Logan found that volunteering brought joy and purpose that directly countered his depression. He noted: 'The one thing that I've found really helps my depression is that I do a lot of volunteering now.' He also stated: 'seeing the smiles on kids' faces or seeing people come up to you and, like, oh, thank you for cleaning up this area. It was getting massive. That's my high.'

pending_qa.q: Why do construction workers historically distrust safety personnel despite their protective intent?
pending_qa.r: Workers view safety staff as obstacles to productivity and job security rather than protectors. Logan explained: 'they never want you or they always say, oh, I hate that safety guy until they need you... the company says they care about safety and they've got all these safety rules, but they don't really sell it as that being the priority. And I knew that if I didn't get my job done well enough, and fast enough, I had job insecurity, right? So the two things always felt kind of at odds.'

pending_qa.q: What is the connection between law enforcement experience and understanding addiction's root causes?
pending_qa.r: From his law enforcement background, Logan recognized that addiction stems from underlying mental health issues rather than being the primary problem itself. He said: 'I noticed with addiction, with alcohol and drugs, that it all stems from something. And a lot of it stems from the whole, I have depression or I have mental illness. We concentrate and we focus so much on the abuse that alcohol and drugs gives, but we never really focus on the cause.'

pending_qa.q: How long have mental health initiatives existed in construction, and what changed in recent years?

He observed: 'Todd put together a mental health program 21 years ago, I think... and it just didn't get the uptake that they wanted. And so it's inspiring to see now that there's such a focus on this. And I think it's also heartbreaking. The reality is that things tipped so far that we just can't ignore it now.'
